name: pickup-spawn
demonstrates: PickupManager schedules the first pickup spawn ~8s after a run begins (per PickupManagerTests) and each pickup persists for a ~20s lifetime, placed on a street tile clear of adjacent buildings (per the placement-search rules pinned by PickupIntegrationTests). This journey waits ~12s past PLAY (past the 8s first-spawn delay with margin for the placement search and frame timing) and takes a screenshot labelled pickup-spawned, reviewed for a small bobbing med-kit or garbage-can icon rendered over an accent-tinted pad -- the tint sits on the pad only, never on the icon itself -- sitting on a street tile and depth-sorted correctly next to any nearby building (not overlapping or drawn behind it), with med kits and garbage cans visually distinguishable from one another. It then waits a further ~6s (now ~18s past PLAY, inside the pickup's lifetime window and past a plausible player-collection window) and takes a second screenshot labelled pickup-lifecycle, reviewed to confirm the pickup is still on the street and still bobbing ~6s later -- the same pickup that spawned at ~8s, or a cleared pad if the player happened to collect it in between -- rather than a sprite that vanishes the moment after it appears. Recurrence and replacement are deliberately NOT claimed for this frame: by the cadence arithmetic below, no second spawn can occur before ~PLAY+33s, so these two screenshots necessarily show the same pickup ~6s apart; that the scheduler keeps producing further pickups after the first is pinned by PickupManagerTests, not observable in these frames. That second wait targets ~18s rather than the ~22s an earlier draft used, because the frozen numbers in PickupKind.tuningTable leave a recurring EMPTY window that a later frame can fall into: cadence (25s) is longer than lifetime (20s) and a kind's cadence re-arms only after a successful spawn, so the effective ceiling is one pickup at a time -- the first pickup expires at ~PLAY+28s and the next one cannot appear before ~PLAY+33s (see the PickupKind.Tuning.maxAlive doc note). navigate is vision-located and each wait starts only after the previous step returns, so ~18s keeps roughly 10s of cumulative slop in hand before that 28-33s dead zone. A reviewer who still lands on an empty street in this frame should read it as that timing artifact rather than as a regression. Camera-independence is explicitly NOT claimed by these screenshots: no step here moves the camera (this journey's action vocabulary is wait / assert_running / screenshot / navigate), so the player stands at the spawn junction for the whole run and the frames cannot distinguish "lifetime is aged by deltaTime only" from "the pickup survived because the camera never moved". That property -- a pickup is never deleted merely because the camera moved -- is pinned by PickupManagerTests.test_largeVisibleRectJumpBetweenUpdates_doesNotAffectPickupAging, which teleports visibleRect a million points between two update calls and asserts expiry still lands on real accumulated deltaTime. Gate is human/vision review of both screenshots; assert_running steps only confirm the app process is still alive. The underlying spawn timing, placement rules, bobbing/tinted rendering, collection and depth-sort behavior are already pinned by PickupManagerTests, PickupNodeTests, PickupIntegrationTests, RaccoonPickupDiversionTests and PlayerHealTests -- this journey exists purely so the runtime probe captures frames late enough for a pickup to actually be on screen, instead of the menu-to-gameplay journey's 5s screenshot which fires well before the first pickup can possibly exist. TWO PROBE RUNS HAVE INSTEAD REPORTED THE APP PROCESS GONE right around PLAY+12s and PLAY+18s, i.e. shortly after PickupKind.medKit/garbageCan's shared 8s firstSpawnDelay fires -- the moment the first Pickup record is created and the first PickupNode is mounted into GameScene -- with two independent static audits of PickupManager/PickupNode/PickupKind/AtlasSheet.pickups/DepthBanding/GameScene's pickup wiring/RaccoonSeekBehavior's diversion path finding no reachable crash site. Rather than re-adding a signal-handler crash-capture harness (tried once already on the near-identical CYBERPUN-17-10 pulse-ability crash: shipped, then removed at close-out as un-owned scaffolding once its own named removal ticket was never filed, with the crash still unidentified -- see the CYBERPUN-17-10/CYBERPUN-17-11 entries in CLAUDE.md), the original 12s/18s single waits are now SPLIT so assert_running brackets the 8s delay: wait 7 (PLAY+7s, before the delay can fire) -> assert_running -> wait 1 (PLAY+8s, the delay fires -- first Pickup created / first PickupNode mounted) -> assert_running -> wait 4 (back to the original PLAY+12s) -> screenshot pickup-spawned -> assert_running -> wait 6 (PLAY+18s) -> screenshot pickup-lifecycle -> assert_running. Total elapsed time and both screenshot timings are UNCHANGED from before; only the bisection checkpoints are new. This does not fix or even localize the crash -- it narrows what the NEXT 'process gone' report can say: died before the delay ever fires (nothing pickup-related is even reached), died right as the first pickup is created/mounted (implicates that exact code path), or survived past it (implicates something later, e.g. player collection or a second update tick). JourneyManifestTests.test_thePickupSpawnJourney_bisectsTheFirstSpawnDelayWithAssertRunningCheckpoints pins both checkpoints against PickupKind.medKit.tuning.firstSpawnDelay so a future retune of the delay, or a trim of these waits back to the old single-step shape, fails in-suite instead of silently losing the bisection.

steps.target: the large neon-outlined PLAY button in the middle of the title screen that starts a new run (NOT the plain HIGH SCORES button below it)
steps.expect: the running game -- a playable isometric city scene with a ground lattice, buildings and a player actor, not a menu or title screen
